qs.q: What is the primary pathological feature in Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)?
o: Extracellular PrP deposits in the cerebellum
Spongiform transformation of the cerebral cortex and deep gray matter
Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra
qs.e: The pathognomonic feature of CJD is the spongiform transformation of the cerebral cortex and deep gray matter, characterized by small vacuoles in the neuropil and neuronal perikarya. Extracellular PrP deposits (Kuru plaques) are mainly in the cerebellum, tau tangles are in Alzheimer's, and substantia nigra degeneration is in Parkinson's.
qs.s: Neurodegenerative Prion Diseases: CJD, Pathology & Rapid Dementia — Notes: MCQs

qs.q: What is the typical clinical presentation of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)?
o: Insidious onset of memory impairment followed by visuospatial deficits
Rapidly progressive dementia with startle myoclonus
Cerebellar ataxia with slow progression over many years
qs.e: CJD is characterized by rapidly progressive dementia, often accompanied by startle myoclonus, which is an involuntary jerking on sudden stimulation. Alzheimer's disease has an insidious onset of memory impairment, Parkinson's disease presents with tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia, and while ataxia can occur in CJD, the rapid dementia is the defining feature.

qs.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of the inflammation in Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)?
o: It is a prominent feature, with significant lymphocytic infiltration.
It is typically absent, which is an important distinguishing feature.
It is characterized by the presence of microglial nodules.
It is primarily mediated by antibodies against PrPsc.
qs.e: Inflammation is notably absent in Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, making this an important distinguishing feature from other neurodegenerative conditions. While microglial activation can occur in neurodegeneration, prominent inflammation is not a hallmark of CJD, and antibody-mediated inflammation is not the primary mechanism described.

qs.q: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), Kuru, scrapie, and Mad Cow disease are caused by
o: Diseases caused primarily by infectious viroids
Diseases caused primarily by active retroviruses
Diseases caused primarily by complex DNA viruses
Diseases caused primarily by pathogenic prions
Diseases caused primarily by single RNA viruses
qs.e: Prions are misfolded proteins (PrP^Sc) that cause fatal neurodegenerative spongiform encephalopathies. They contain no nucleic acid — making them unique among all known infectious agents. They are extraordinarily resistant to heat, radiation, and standard disinfection. CJD, Kuru, scrapie (sheep), and variant CJD (Mad Cow) are all prion diseases.
